evidence.experimental_conditions: 10 female albino guinea pigs (Himalayan strain, 4 weeks old, SPF-quality) test group; 5 female guinea pigs controls; intradermally injected and epidermally exposed to undiluted D6; challenged with undiluted D6 (first challenge) and 50% and 20% D6 (second challenge); 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate pretreatment 24 hours before epidermal induction; vehicle corn oil.
evidence.support_text: Pels Rijcken studied the skin sensitization potential of D6 using the maximization test. Ten female albino guinea pigs (Himalayan strain, 4 weeks old, SPF-quality) comprised the test group, and 5 female guinea pigs served as controls (corn oil = control). The test animals were intradermally injected and epidermally exposed to undiluted D6, and the 5 control guinea pigs were treated similarly with corn oil. Approximately 24 hours prior to epidermal induction exposure, all of the animals were treated with 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate. At 2 weeks after epidermal application, all of the animals were challenged with undiluted D6 and the vehicle. One week later, the animals were subjected to a second challenge with 50% D6 and 20% D6. Following the first challenge, grade 1 skin reactions were observed among 3 test animals and 1 control animal in response to undiluted D6. After the second challenge, no reactions to 50% D6 or 20% D6 were observed. Based on the results of the second challenge phase, it was concluded that there was no evidence that D6 had caused skin hypersensitivity in guinea pigs. These results indicate a sensitization rate of 0%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig maximization test; induction with SCAOP; occluded patch challenge with SCAOP; 24h and 48h readings
evidence.support_text: From Table II, in guinea pig maximization tests, animals induced with SCAOP showed positive skin reactions when challenged with SCAOP (challenge 3: 90% at 24h and 80% at 48h; earlier challenges also positive). The reactions were severe with oedema and necrosis at second challenge.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig maximization test; MC903 ointment applied with adjuvant to enhance sensitivity.
evidence.support_text: Considering that the Maximization test used in this study is a test method that enhances sensitivity to sensitization by co-sensitizing adjuvant with the test substance, MC903 ointment was considered to show almost no sensitization to guinea pig skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig maximization test; sensitization with DNCB, challenge with 0.1% DNCB in white petrolatum; skin reactions observed at 24 and 48 hours.
evidence.support_text: On the other hand, at the site where sensitization was induced with the positive control substance DNCB and challenge was performed with 0.1% DNCB white petrolatum ointment, clear skin reactions were observed at 24 and 48 hours, respectively, confirming the validity of the test system.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig model; no further details reported
evidence.support_text: Already MBPA showed an alert of skin sensitization for phenols. In various skin sensitization assays including the guinea pig maximization test and the human maximization test this effect was demonstrated [72,73].

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, 1 mg/0.2 ml difluprednate, 24-hour closed patch on flank, observation 24 h after patch removal
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, 12 guinea pigs were sensitized with difluprednate and challenged with 1 mg/0.2 ml difluprednate by 24-hour closed patch on the flank. Observation 24 h after patch removal showed no contact allergic reaction in any animal (score 0).
